verification_level: FAST plus BATCH; no STOP (no confirmed UB left unrepaired, no ABI regression, no hidden obligation and no remaining unsafe-safe-Rust API); two soundness/aliasing repairs, three argument-ordering repairs, one failure-path leak repair and one overflow repair
scope: Per-file contract audit of GCM, the non-AEAD mode helpers (CBC/OFB/CFB/CTR/CTS), OCB, AES-SIV, RFC 3394/5649 key wrap, XTS and the OCSP client plus OCSP HTTP client. evp/method_store.rs was deferred again as the method-store registry boundary; ocsp/ocsp_http.rs was substituted from the head of the stable queue. AEAD/IV/tag and wrap intermediates are classified as secret or security-critical; no constant-time claim is made for any file from source inspection.

files_not_run.reason: Method-store registry and OSSL_METHOD_CONSTRUCT_METHOD dispatch boundary (store locking, construct/reserve/unreserve callbacks, method cache). Deferred for a dedicated boundary audit; it remains in REMAINING-AUDIT.txt at the head of the queue.

defects.class: safe Rust function dereferences a caller-supplied raw pointer (unsafe-safe-Rust API)
defects.description: ctr128_inc and ctr96_inc were plain safe fns taking *mut u8 and dereferencing it, so a safe caller inside the crate could pass NULL and cause undefined behaviour.
defects.fix: Both are now unsafe fn with a # Safety contract requiring a writable sixteen-byte counter; the four in-file call sites carry SAFETY comments. The authority's arithmetic is unchanged.
defects.witness: focused modes:: tests (25) and the full library suite pass.

defects.class: overlapping shared/mutable references in the in-place partial-block arm
defects.description: CRYPTO_ocb128_encrypt and CRYPTO_ocb128_decrypt formed from_raw_parts(inp, last_len) and from_raw_parts_mut(outp, last_len) over the same range whenever in == out, which EVP's block update may pass. Simultaneous &/&mut over one range is undefined behaviour even though the byte loop is read-then-write. The full-block arms already use a local copy.
defects.fix: The input tail is copied into a local [u8; 16] before the output is mutably borrowed; encrypt checksums the preserved plaintext, decrypt still checksums the written plaintext as the authority does. New regression test ocb_partial_block_in_place_matches_out_of_place pins bytes and tag against the out-of-place result.
defects.witness: modes::ocb tests, including the new in-place test, and the full library suite pass.

defects.class: size arithmetic before the length range test (debug-build panic across the C ABI)
defects.description: crypto_128_unwrap_raw evaluated inlen - 8 before the range test. A caller-supplied inlen below eight underflowed: the authority's unsigned subtraction wraps and is then rejected, but the Rust debug build panicked and aborted.
defects.fix: checked_sub(8) with a zero (refusal) answer for the short arm. Observable release behaviour is unchanged.
defects.witness: New modes::wrap test out_of_range_lengths_are_refused_before_pointer_use passes with NULL buffers.

defects.class: size arithmetic before the length range test (debug-build panic across the C ABI)
defects.description: CRYPTO_128_wrap_pad computed blocks_padded = inlen.div_ceil(8) and padded_len = blocks_padded * 8 before testing inlen == 0 || inlen >= CRYPTO128_WRAP_MAX; a huge caller length overflowed the multiply in a debug build.
defects.fix: The authority's range test now runs before the ceiling arithmetic.
defects.witness: New modes::wrap test includes inlen == usize::MAX and inlen == 0 with NULL buffers.

defects.class: size arithmetic before the length range test (debug-build panic across the C ABI)
defects.description: CRYPTO_128_unwrap_pad evaluated n = inlen / 8 - 1 before the range test; inlen below eight underflowed in a debug build.
defects.fix: The range test now precedes the block count.
defects.witness: New modes::wrap test passes inlen == 7 with NULL buffers.

defects.class: failure-path resource leak and half-built state
defects.description: OCSP_request_sign's key-mismatch arm returned 0 with the freshly created OCSP_SIGNATURE still installed on the request. The authority's goto err frees that signature and clears req->optionalSignature.
defects.fix: The arm frees the signature and nulls the pointer before returning, matching the authority's error path.
defects.witness: Contract review; the arm needs a mismatched key pair and is not exercised by a unit test (runtime control NOT_RUN).

defects.class: integer overflow in a caller-controlled scan bound (debug-build panic across the C ABI)
defects.description: OCSP_resp_find computed last + 1; last == INT_MAX overflowed in a debug build. The authority's signed addition is undefined for that value.
defects.fix: saturating_add(1): the scan is empty and the answer is -1, the same answer the release build produced by wrapping.

contracts_reused: Validated-initialisation owner transition and single cleansing release: GcmRawCtx (block-only Drop, authority CRYPTO_free at gcm128.c:1616) to GcmCtxOwner (CRYPTO_clear_free over sizeof(GcmCtx))
RawCtx/CtxDestroy for OcbCtx and Siv128Context: destroy_body releases owned members and cleanses the context, never the enclosing block
OCB L-table member extent: CRYPTO_clear_free(l, max_l_index * 16); copy_ctx copies l_index + 1 populated entries into a max_l_index-sized block; lookup_l grows before writing
Caller-populated #[repr(C)] XTS128_CONTEXT (key1/key2/block1/block2) and the caller's in/out/iv extent contracts
C ABI caller contracts for ctx liveness, NULL-or-live optional pointers and in-place operation, plus the CRYPTO_* allocator seam at the authority's FILE/LINE coordinates
Authority 3.6.4 source semantics for gcm128.c, ctr128.c, cfb128.c, cts128.c, ocb128.c, siv128.c, wrap128.c, xts128.c and ocsp_cl.c
residuals: src/evp/method_store.rs remains the deferred method-store registry / OSSL_METHOD_CONSTRUCT_METHOD dispatch boundary.

OCSP_request_sign's set1_name-failure arm returns without freeing a pre-existing optionalSignature, whereas the authority's goto err frees it and clears the pointer. The Rust arm is safer and is reachable only on an allocation failure; recorded as a divergence.

OCSP_check_validity still evaluates t_now + nsec and t_now - maxsec without checked arithmetic. nsec/maxsec are caller configuration rather than network data and the authority's signed overflow is undefined; hardening candidate.

The in-place OCB partial-block tag now checksums the original plaintext. The authority's C reads in after writing out, so an exactly-overlapping caller would checksum ciphertext and produce a different tag; the safe result is retained and pinned by a regression test, and non-overlapping behaviour is identical.
wrap.rs locals a/b, OCB pad/tail and SIV locals t/q are not cleansed, as the authority also leaves them; they are keyed intermediates, not key stores.
No constant-time claim is made for GCM, OCB, AES-SIV, key wrap or XTS from source inspection; dudect/ctgrind remain BOUNDARY/SEAL work.
